key_insight: The Cornucopia architecture turns an ultra-high-rate quantum memory code into a modular fault-tolerant processor by adding low-overhead reusable logical-operation gadgets.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical path to scalable quantum computers that preserve the memory efficiency of high-rate codes while still supporting universal logical computation on individually addressable logical qubits.
method: Use the [[2844,1426,18]] Cornucopia code as the module-level memory and processor block.
Connect code blocks with bridges to form a modular architecture.
Exploit translation symmetry to build reusable gadgets for universal logical instruction sets with low ancilla overhead.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that a basic-instruction module needs an average of 4.1 physical qubits per logical qubit, versus 3.0 for memory alone, while still supporting 1,426 logical qubits per block and 1,422 individually addressable qubits.
watch_item: The claimed overhead advantage depends on excluding magic-state factories, so full system-level cost may be higher in a complete fault-tolerant implementation.
paper_title: A modular quantum computer based on Cornucopia codes
